topics.title: Care of the Hair - Types of Hair Infection | Effects of Sharing Unsterilized Instruments when Barbing Hair Primary 3 (Basic 3) - Home Economics
topics.content:
HOME ECONOMICS
PREVOCATIONAL STUDIES
SECOND TERM
WEEK 3
PRIMARY 3
THEME - HEALTHY LIVING
PREVIOUS LESSON - Care of the Hair - Types of Hair | Articles for Cleaning Hair | Types of Hair Infection | Primary 3 (Basic 3) - Home Economics
TOPIC - CARE OF THE HAIR
LEARNING AREA
1. Introductory Activities
2. Types of Hair Infection
3. Effects of Sharing Unsterilized Instruments when Barbing Hair
4. Lesson Evaluation and Weekly Assessment (Test)
PERFORMANCE OBJECTIVES
By the end of the lesson, the pupils should have attained the following objectives (cognitive, affective and psychomotor) and should be able to -
state the effects of sharing unsterilized instruments when barbing hair.
ENTRY BEHAVIOUR
The pupils can state the different hair infection.
INSTRUCTIONAL MATERIALS
The teacher will teach the lesson with the aid of:
1. Comb, brush, soap, shampoo, water, cream, towel, basin, etc.
2. Sample of artificial hairs.
3. With the school permission, asks the pupils (mostly the girls) to come with free style hairs. It is optional.
METHOD OF TEACHING
Choose a suitable and appropriate methods for the lessons.
Note - Irrespective of choosing methods of teaching, always introduce an activities that will arouse pupil’s interest or lead them to the lessons.
REFERENCE MATERIALS
1. Scheme of Work
2. 9 - Years Basic Education Curriculum
3. Course Book
4. All Relevant Material
5. Online Information
CONTENT OF THE LESSON
LESSON 1 - INTRODUCTORY ACTIVITIES
Teacher’s Activities - Display charts showing different types of hair infection for the pupils to identify and discuss.
Pupil’s Activities - Participate in the discussion.
Teacher’s remark - Listen to the pupils and note the points on the board and discuss.
Copy as I write on board.
TYPES OF HAIR INFECTIONS
1. Rashes
2. Lice
3. Ringworm
4. Dandruff, etc.
LESSON 2 - INTRODUCTORY ACTIVITIES
Teacher’s Activities - Teacher’s/Pupil’s Activities - Discuss the effects of sharp unsterilized instruments as discussed in hair infections. Also, mention HIV/AIDS as the worst hair infection.
Pupil’s Activities - Participate actively in the discussion.
Teacher’s remark - For active participation, give a great cheer. Note the points of discussion on the board for the pupils to copy.
EFFECTS OF SHARING UNSTERILIZED BARBING INSTRUMENT
1. Risk of contacting HIV/AIDS.
2. Exposure to germs such as ringworm, etc.
3. itching
4. Tetanus
5. Lice
PRESENTATION
To deliver the lesson, the teacher adopts the following steps:
1. To introduce the lesson, the teacher revises the previous lesson. Based on this, he/she asks the pupils some questions;
2. Guide the pupils to state the hair infection.
Pupil’s Activities - State the hair infection.
3. Informs pupils about HIV/AIDS and how it can be contacted from poor use of instruments during barbing or during shampooing at salons.
Pupil’s Activities - Get information on how HIV?AIDS can be contacted in salons and barbing centers.
4. Summarizes the lesson on the board.
Pupil’s Activities - Copy as the teacher writes.
CONCLUSION
To conclude the lesson for the week, the teacher revises the entire lesson and links it to the following week’s lesson.
NEXT LESSON
LESSON EVALUATION
Ask pupils to:
1. name two hair infection that could be contacted at salons and barbing centers.
3. state three reasons why we should not share hair care articles or tools.

topics.title: Care of the Hair - Types of Hair | Articles for Cleaning Hair | Types of Hair Infection | Primary 3 (Basic 3) - Home Economics
topics.content:
HOME ECONOMICS
PREVOCATIONAL STUDIES
SECOND TERM
WEEK 2
PRIMARY 3
THEME - HEALTHY LIVING
PREVIOUS LESSON - Exam Questions - First Term Examination Home Economics Primary 3 (Basic 3)
TOPIC - CARE OF THE HAIR
LEARNING AREA
1. Introductory Activities
2. Process of Caring for Different Types of Hair
3. Hair Infections
4. Materials Needed for Hair Care
5. Lesson Evaluation and Weekly Assessment (Test)
PERFORMANCE OBJECTIVES
By the end of the lesson, the pupils should have attained the following objectives (cognitive, affective and psychomotor) and should be able to -
1. identify different types of hair and explain the process of caring for them.
2. mention hair infections.
3. list materials used in hair care.
4. keep well cut and groomed hair.
ENTRY BEHAVIOUR
The pupils can identify human and animal hair.
INSTRUCTIONAL MATERIALS
The teacher will teach the lesson with the aid of:
1. Comb, brush, soap, shampoo, water, cream, towel, basin, etc.
2. Sample of artificial hairs.
3. With the school permission, asks the pupils (mostly the girls) to come with free style hairs. It is optional.
METHOD OF TEACHING
Choose a suitable and appropriate methods for the lessons.
Note - Irrespective of choosing methods of teaching, always introduce an activities that will arouse pupil’s interest or lead them to the lessons.
REFERENCE MATERIALS
1. Scheme of Work
2. 9 - Years Basic Education Curriculum
3. Course Book
4. All Relevant Material
5. Online Information
WRITING INSTRUCTION
Copy as I write or draw as I write. This instruction should be given when you need the pupils to write or draw.
CONTENT OF THE LESSON
INTRODUCTORY ACTIVITIES
Teacher’s Activities - Call out some pupils with unique type of hair (if available) or display charts showing natural hair for the to identify the difference.
Pupil’s Activities - Response to teacher’s instructions.
Teacher’s remarks - A great cheer for quick response. Continue discussion on types of hair and ask pupils to state materials needed for hair care and cleaning.
Copy as I write on board.
TYPES OF HAIR
There are different types of hair and they are -
1. Straight hair
2. Wavy hair
3. Curly hair
4. Coiled hair
5. Zig zag hair
ARTICLES USED FOR HAIR CARE AND CLEANING
Materials needed for hair care and cleaning are -
1.Comb
2. Brush
3. Pomade or cream
4. Mirror
5. Shampoo
6. Curling materials, etc.
LESSON 2 - PRACTICAL DEMONSTRATION OF HOW TO CARE AND CLEAN THE HAIR
Teacher’s/Pupil’s Activities - To avoid hair infections, there is need to regularly clean and take care of the hair daily. Guide the pupils to demonstrate how to clean and take care of their hair.
PRESENTATION
To deliver the lesson, the teacher adopts the following steps:
1. To introduce the lesson, the teacher revises the previous lesson. Based on this, he/she asks the pupils some questions;
2. Discuss types of hair.
Pupil’s Activities - Participate actively in the discussion.
3. Guide the pupils to state the hair infection.
Pupil’s Activities - State the hair infection.
4. Assembles materials for hair care articles.
Pupil’s Activities - Help assemble hair care materials on table.
3. Demonstrates how to use them.
Pupil’s Activities - Wash, comb and brush their hair, clean and tidy up after demonstration.
4. Summarizes the lesson on the board.
Pupil’s Activities - Copy as the teacher writes.
CONCLUSION
To conclude the lesson for the week, the teacher revises the entire lesson and links it to the following week’s lesson.
NEXT LESSON
Care of the Hair - Types of Hair Infection | Effects of Sharing Unsterilized Instruments when Barbing Hair Primary 3 (Basic 3) - Home Economics
LESSON EVALUATION
Ask pupils to:
1. list those things used for caring for hair.
2. name two hair infection that could be contacted at salons and barbing centers.

HOME ECONOMICS

TOPIC - CARE OF THE SKIN
LEARNING AREA
1. Introductory Activities
2. Skin Infections and Diseases
3. Prevention and Care of Skin Infections
4. Lesson Evaluation and Weekly Assessment (Test)
PERFORMANCE OBJECTIVES
By the end of the lesson, the pupils should have attained the following objectives (cognitive, affective and psychomotor) and should be able to -
1. mention different skin infections and diseases.
2. state ways of preventing skin infections and diseases.
ENTRY BEHAVIOUR
The pupils can demonstrate how to take care of the skin.
INSTRUCTIONAL MATERIALS
The teacher will teach the lesson with the aid of:
1. Chart showing skin care articles.
2. Real objects e.g. soap, powder, perfume, deodorants, hena, camwood.
3. Pictures of skin infections/diseases.
METHOD OF TEACHING
Choose a suitable and appropriate methods for the lessons.
Note - Irrespective of choosing methods of teaching, always introduce an activities that will arouse pupil’s interest or lead them to the lessons.
REFERENCE MATERIALS
1. Scheme of Work
2. 9 - Years Basic Education Curriculum
3. Course Book
4. All Relevant Material
5. Online Information
WRITING INSTRUCTION
Copy as I write or draw as I write. This instruction should be given when you need the pupils to write or draw.
CONTENT OF THE LESSON
LESSON 1 - INTRODUCTORY ACTIVITIES
Teacher’s Activities - Display charts showing different types of skin infections for the pupils to identify and guide them to describe.
Pupil’s Activities - Participate in the discussion.
Teacher’s remark - Give a great cheer for active participation and note the skin infections and diseases as identified and discuss.
Copy as I write on the board.
SKIN INFECTIONS AND DISEASE
Common skin infections and diseases are -
1. Boils
2. Ringworm
3. Athletes foot
4. Razor Bumps
5. Eczema
LESSON 2 - INTRODUCTORY ACTIVITIES
Teacher’s Activities - Ask the pupils how to prevent some common skin infections and diseases.
Pupil’s Activities - Taking bath regularly, etc.
Teacher’s remark - Give a great cheer for quick response and note the pupils points on the board.
Copy as I write on the board.
PREVENTION AND CARE OF THE SKIN INFECTIONS
1. Bathing with clean water.
2. Eating balanced diet.
3. Wearing clean clothes.
4. Avoid sharing body articles like towel,sponge, comb, etc.
5. Avoid playing with dirty water.
6. Use appropriate skin cream.
7. Regular exercise.
PRESENTATION
To deliver the lesson, the teacher adopts the following steps:
1. To introduce the lesson, the teacher revises the previous lesson. Based on this, he/she asks the pupils some questions;
2. Discuss skin infections and disease and how to prevent them.
Pupil’s Activities - Explain how to prevent skin infections and diseases.
3. Summarizes the lesson on the board.
Pupil’s Activities - Copy as the teacher writes.
CONCLUSION
To conclude the lesson for the week, the teacher revises the entire lesson and links it to the following week’s lesson.
NEXT LESSON
Uses of Clothes | Care of Clothes Primary 3 (Basic 3)
LESSON EVALUATION
Ask pupils to:
1. mention 3 skin infections and diseases.
2. state 3 ways of preventing skin infections and diseases.

1. Brushes, dusters, brooms, (long and short broom).

Pupil’s Activities - Sitting room, bedroom, etc.
Teacher’s remark - A great cheer for quick response. There are different rooms in a house. Bedroom is one of them. Ask the pupils to describe and guide them to state the reasons for cleaning the bedroom.
REASONS FOR CLEANING THE BEDROOM
Bedroom is a private that people for sleeping during or relaxing during the day. Cleaning the bedroom makes the bedroom to be -
1. Tidiness
2. Free flow of air.
3. Free from dust.
4. Conducive for rest and sleep.
LESSON 2 - INTRODUCTORY ACTIVITIES
Teacher’s/Pupil’s Activities - Ask the pupils to state the materials used for cleaning the bedroom. Note their points on the board and discuss how each materials are used.

2. Water
3. Soap and detergents
4. Polish
5. Dust pan
6. Dust bin
7. Mattress, pillow and cases, bed sheet, bed ( improvised).
PRESENTATION
To deliver the lesson, the teacher adopts the following steps:
1. To introduce the lesson, the teacher revises the previous lesson. Based on this, he/she asks the pupils some questions;
2. Guides pupils to state the reasons for the cleaning of the bedroom.
Pupil’s Activities - State reasons for the cleaning of the bedroom.
3. Provides all the cleaning materials and explain and how they are used.
Pupil’s Activities - Help in gathering materials for cleaning.
4. Summarizes the lesson on the board.
Pupil’s Activities - Copy as the teacher writes.
CONCLUSION
To conclude the lesson for the week, the teacher revises the entire lesson and links it to the following week’s lesson.

PRIMARY 3
THEME - FOOD AND NUTRITION AND HEALTH
PREVIOUS LESSON - Functions of Food | Foods Belongings to Various Food Groups (Primary 3)
TOPIC - FOODS GROUP
LEARNING AREA
1. Introductory Activities
2. Foodstuffs that Belong to More than One Group
3. Lesson Evaluation and Weekly Assessment (Test)
PERFORMANCE OBJECTIVES
By the end of the lesson, the pupils should have attained the following objectives (cognitive, affective and psychomotor) and should be able to -
identify foodstuff that belong to more than one group.
ENTRY BEHAVIOUR
The pupils can identify foodstuff in the locality according to their functions.
INSTRUCTIONAL MATERIALS
The teacher will teach the lesson with the aid of:
1. Samples of foodstuff mentioned e.g. yam, eggs, meat, fruits, vegetable, etc.
2. Chart on foodstuffs that appear in various groups.-Proteins, Fats,
Carbohydrates, Minerals, Vitamins.
METHOD OF TEACHING
Choose a suitable and appropriate methods for the lessons.
Note - Irrespective of choosing methods of teaching, always introduce an activities that will arouse pupil’s interest or lead them to the lessons.
REFERENCE MATERIALS
1. Scheme of Work
2. 9 - Years Basic Education Curriculum
3. Course Book
4. All Relevant Material
5. Online Information
WRITING INSTRUCTION
Copy as I write or draw as I write. This instruction should be given when you need the pupils to write or draw.
CONTENT OF THE LESSON
LESSON 2 - INTRODUCTORY ACTIVITIES
Teacher’s/Pupil’s Activities - Discuss the source of different functions of food.
SOURCES OF FOOD
1. Body building foods
Source - Meat, fish, beans, soyabean, etc.
2. Energy giving foods
Source - Yam, garri, bread, potatoes, etc.
3. Protective foods
Source - Orange, banana, green vegetables, etc.
4. Maintenance foods
Source - Liver, kidney, crayfish, crab, etc.
LESSON 2 - FOODS THAT BELONG TO MORE THAN ONE GROUP
Teacher’s/Pupil’s Activities - Discuss briefly why the foods belong to more than one group and itemise some foods that belong to more than one group for the pupils to sort from the chart.
1. Eggs - Protein, Vitamins, etc.
2. Fruit - Fruits - Vitamins and Minerals
3. Rice -
4. Vegetables -
5. Beans -
6. Soybeans
7. Meat, etc.
PRESENTATION
To deliver the lesson, the teacher adopts the following steps:
1. To introduce the lesson, the teacher revises the previous lesson. Based on this, he/she asks the pupils some questions;
2. Leads pupils to itemise source of different functions of food.
3. Discuss briefly why the foods belong to more than one group, that is contain protein, fat, carbohydrate, vitamins and minerals in certain.
Pupil’s Activities - Active participation in the discussion.
4. Summarizes the lesson on the board.
Pupil’s Activities - Copy as the teacher writes.
CONCLUSION
To conclude the lesson for the week, the teacher revises the entire lesson and links it to the following week’s lesson.
NEXT LESSON
Revision and Second Term Examination Home Economics Basic 3
LESSON EVALUATION
Ask pupils to mention 4 foodstuffs that belong to more than one group.
